chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskaan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Umrah of the one who is tested (or: the Umrah performed with a specific condition/ruling) — he performs Tawaf by the House (Kaaba), and by Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, then he frees himself from Ihram. So if he desires to depart from that moment, he departs.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (one of the hills for Sa'i)
key_terms.الْعُمْرَةُ الْمَبْتُولَةُ: The Umrah of the tested/conditioned (a specific juristic category of Umrah)
key_terms.يَحِلُّ: He frees himself (from the state of Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for exiting Ihram after performing Umaf and Sa'i in the specific Umrah mentioned in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the ruling for 'Al-Mabtoolah' (often equated with Umrah Tamattu'), where the pilgrim performs Tawaf and Sa'i but does not perform the Qasr prayer or full haircut within the Umrah rites, thereby exiting the state of Ihram immediately. This distinguishes it from Umrah Mufradah and highlights the flexibility in concluding the pilgrimage rites, a point of emphasis in Usuli fiqh regarding the separation of Hajj and Umrah obligations.
